biodiversity_overview.text: 750 GBIF occurrence records for 18 tracked species are attributed to Nagaland, spanning 1886-2025.
734 of these records (97.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 9, Magnoliopsida 5, Mammalia 2, Liliopsida 1, Amphibia 1.

threatened_species.text: 2 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Blue Robin (350), Indian White-eye (303), Indian Cuckoo (46), Mango (15), Indian Gooseberry (7).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 21 in 2016 to 6 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 2.3% of Nagaland's area (6 areas intersect the state).
1.2% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (9 of 734); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Dwarf Banana (0.55), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Bulletwood (0.30), Acacia-tree (0.26), Bull Frog (0.24).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Nagaland (equal-weight reference): cell near 25.875N 94.125E (overall rank 282, median rank across weightings 288); cell near 25.875N 94.875E (overall rank 342, median rank across weightings 342).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 13,614 km2 (79.18% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

2,725.1 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (20.02% of the 2000 extent; 10.65% in 2015-2024, rank 3 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2017 (210.54 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.35% of land and population density is 115.1 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
14% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
